action.message:
I was unable to land the required behavioral fix within the request budget.

What happened: the target condition in `BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py`, lines 467-470) was never actually changed. My edit attempts either resubmitted identical old/new strings (rejected as "old_str equals new_str") or only touched surrounding whitespace/blank lines. As a result the logic still reads:

    if not prev_field or (
        prev_field.is_relation
        and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
    ):
        relation_parts.append(part)

Root cause (confirmed by reading `ForeignObject.get_path_info` in `django/db/models/fields/related.py:817-835`): `target_fields` is `self.foreign_related_fields`. For `Restaurant.place` being a `OneToOneField(primary_key=True)`, `Restaurant.id` resolves to the `place` field itself, so when processing `restaurant__place__country`, the `place` segment is found in `restaurant.path_infos[-1].target_fields` and is skipped — collapsing the lookup to `restaurant__country`, which is not in `list_filter`, so `lookup_allowed` returns False.

The intended fix (not applied) was to only skip the segment when the field is not itself a relation, e.g.:

    if not prev_field or (
        prev_field.is_relation
        and field not in prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields
        and not field.is_relation
    ):
        relation_parts.append(part)

Verification status: the public regression selection (`modeladmin`) reports passed (162 tests, OK), but this reflects the unchanged original code, NOT a fix. The host feature test `test_lookup_allowed_foreign_primary` still fails (`AssertionError: False is not True`), and I did not land a source change that addresses it. This task is incomplete.
